newsitem.title: USA: Gay "Ellen" tv show biggest U.S. coming out party ever.
newsitem.headline: Gay "Ellen" tv show biggest U.S. coming out party ever.

text.p: U.S. television sitcom character Ellen Morgan finally comes out the closet on Wednesday night to say "I'm gay", and tens of thousands of gays and lesbians will celebrate with her at parties in bars, clubs, community halls and homes across the United States.

The event, a first in which a tv comedy will have a gay lead character, is probably the country's worst-kept sceret. Since the story first broke in TV Guide there has been an avalanche of hype and hoopla, and a little controversy.

Gay groups say it is a landmark and have planned what is probably the biggest coming out party in the world for Ellen, played by comedienne Ellen DeGeneres, who has also come out publicly in recent weeks, including on the cover of Time.
The four-year-old ABC show "Ellen" has been struggling in the ratings and up to 20 million people are expected to gather around televison sets for Wednesday's night's historic show.

"I think it is unprecedented in terms of a national celebration by gays, lesbians and their supporters," said Alan Klein, spokesman for the New-York-based Gay and Lesbian Alliance Against Defamation (GLAAD).
"There are parties in every state. I hope you can hear the magic words over the cheers of the crowd," he told Reuters.

GLAAD has organised 1,500 "Come out with Ellen" parties in homes across the country, issuing kits with posters and invitations. It also hosts parties in clubs in Los Angeles, New York, Washington, Kansas, San Diego and San Francisco.

A Los Angeles party will be held at "The Love Lounge" in Beverly Hills with some of the show's cast members expected. A GLAAD staffer in Los Angeles said she did not know if DeGeneres or her new girlfriend, "Volcano" star Anne Heche, would be attending.

In Birmingham, Alabama, where a local affiliate ABC 33/40 has refused to air the episode due to its content, the Birmingham Pride Alabama gay group will downlink the show via satellite to an audience at an "Official Welcome Out Ellen Party" at a city auditorium.

"Finally gay people are part of the American family portrait televison presents," BPA's Kevin Snow said in a statement. "This event shows we will not be cropped out of the picture because of one small-minded station manager."
In Miami, the SAVE gay group set up a hotline telling people where house parties would be held. The organisation was also hosting parties after the show at two night clubs.
In Washington, Candace Gingrich, gay activist and half-sister of House Speaker Newt Gingrich, was expected to attend an Ellen-watching party in a fancy downtown restaurant.

Some big stars are making cameo appearances to give their blessing to the one-hour special, including Laura Dern, who plays the woman Ellen falls for, Demi Moore, k.d. lang and Oprah Winfrey, the talk show host who is a symbol of middle-American sensibility. Winfrey plays Ellen's therapist.
